[[Al Raed FC|Al-Raed]] | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2008–09 Saudi Pro League|2008–09]] | nextseason = [[2010–11 Saudi Pro League|2010–11]] }} The '''2009–10 Saudi Professional League''' (known as the '''[[Zain Group|Zain]] Professional League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 34th season of the [[Saudi Pro League]], the top Saudi professional league for [[association football]] clubs, since its establishment in [[1976–77 Saudi Premier League|1976]]. The season began on 18 August 2009, and ended on 18 March 2010.{{cite web |title=جدول الدوري |url=http://www.slstat.com/spl2009-2010ar/champtable.php |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422161124/http://www.slstat.com/spl2009-2010ar/champtable.php |archivedate=22 April 2016 |url-status=dead}} [[Al-Ittihad Club (Jeddah)|Al-Ittihad]] were the [[2008–09 Saudi Pro League|defending champions]].{{cite web |title=الاتحاد بطلا لدوري المحترفين السعودي بفوزه على الهلال |url=https://www.aleqt.com/2009/04/12/article_215277.html}} [[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]] secured the title with a 2–0 win away to [[Al-Hazem F.C.|Al-Hazem]] on 24 January 2010.{{cite web |title=الهلال بطلاً للدوري السعودي 2010 |url=http://www.alriyadh.com/492692}} Al-Hilal won the league with three games to spare. Al-Hilal, [[Al-Ittihad Club (Jeddah)|Al-Ittihad]], [[Al Shabab FC (Riyadh)|Al-Shabab]] and [[Al-Nassr FC|Al-Nassr]] all secured a berth for the [[2011 AFC Champions League]]. No teams were relegated at the end of the season following the decision to increase the number of teams from 12 to 14.{{cite web |title=هل ستتغير خارطة دوري "زين"؟ |url=http://www.alriyadh.com/553669}} ==Name sponsorship== On 16 June 2009, the Saudi Professional League announced sponsorship agreement with telecommunication company [[Zain Group|Zain]]. As part of the sponsorship deal, the Saudi Professional League would be known as the Zain Professional League for the next 4 seasons.{{cite web |title=تغيير مسمى دوري المحترفين السعودي إلى "دوري زين" |url=https://www.alriyadh.com/438098}} == Qualification and Prize Money == The League champions, runners-up and third-placed team, as well as the winners of the [[2010 King Cup of Champions|King Cup of Champions]], qualify for the [[2011 AFC Champions League]]. The top six teams, and the [[2009–10 Saudi Crown Prince Cup|Crown Prince Cup]] winners and runners-up qualify for [[2010 King Cup of Champions|King Cup of Champions]]. * Prize money: ** First place: 2.5 million Saudi Riyals ** Second place: 1.5 million Saudi Riyals ** Third place: 1 million Saudi Riyals ==Teams== Twelve teams competed in the league – the top nine teams from the previous season, the relegation play-off winner and the two teams promoted from the [[Saudi First Division]]. [[Al Raed FC|Al-Raed]] defeated [[Abha Club|Abha]] 4–3 on aggregate to confirm their top-flight status.{{cite web |title="رائد التحدي" يعلن البقاء في دوري الأضواء |url=https://www.alriyadh.com/426050}} The promoted teams were [[Al Qadsiah FC|Al-Qadsiah]] (returning after a season's absence) and [[Al Fateh SC|Al-Fateh]] (playing top-flight football for the first time ever). They replaced [[Abha Club|Abha]] (relegated after a season's presence) and [[Al-Watani Club|Al-Watani]] (ending their two-year top-flight spell). ===Stadiums and locations=== {{Location map+ |Saudi Arabia |width=440 |float=right |caption=Locations of teams in the 2009–10 Saudi Professional League |places= {{Location map~ |Saudi Arabia |lat=21.54333 |long=39.17278 |label=[[Al-Ahli Saudi FC|Al-Ahli]]
